title: Thickness-Driven Superconductor-Insulator Transition in (Cu,C)-1234 and Proximity-Induced Superconductivity Recovery in (Cu,C)-1234/YBCO Heterostructure
authors: Zhihang Xu, Detian Yang, Ping Zhu, Ruoxian Sun, Xiaoyang Cai, Yanqun Guo, Chuanbing Cai
abstract: Superconducting proximity effect and related thickness-driven property evolution remain an important issue in understanding high temperature superconductors. Among proximity systems, superconductor-superconductor (S-S') is special for the existence of intrinsic superconductivity in both materials. Such platform allows the different superconducting orders to compete, couple and reconstruct at the interface. In this paper, (Cu,C)-1234/YBCO heterostructure grown on LAO (001) with fixed thickness of bottom YBCO layer as 150 nm and varied thickness of top (Cu,C)-1234 layer as 188nm, 87 nm, 18nm and estimated 1.2 nm were fabricated and component films were preserved. Electrical transport characterization indicated that as the thickness decrease the (Cu,C)-1234 film degrades and underwent the superconductor-insulator transition (SIT) from thicker to less than 18 nm. In contrast, superconductivity is re-established in transport measurements when the insulating (Cu,C)-1234 layer is coupled to superconducting YBCO As the (Cu,C)-1234 thickness is further reduced to approximately 1.2 nm, the recovered superconductivity is strongly suppressed. The observed thickness dependence is consistent with a scenario in which interfacial coupling restores superconductivity over a finite thickness range before increasing disorder and dimensional confinement dominate in the two-dimensional limit. This work establishes a promising platform for investigating interfacial coupling between cuprate superconductors and provides new insight into the superconducting proximity effect in high-temperature superconducting heterostructures.
summary: The paper investigates the interplay between thickness-driven Superconductor-Insulator Transition (SIT) and proximity effects in $	ext{(Cu,C)-1234/YBCO}$ heterostructures. By varying the top layer thickness, they observed that while the material undergoes SIT when isolated, coupling it to YBCO restores superconductivity over a specific thickness range. This work establishes a platform for studying interfacial superconducting coupling in high-temperature superconductors.
main_problem: The study investigates the interplay between thickness-driven Superconductor-Insulator Transition (SIT) and superconducting proximity effects in high-temperature cuprate heterostructures.
main_result: Reducing the thickness of the top layer causes an SIT, but superconductivity is re-established across the interface with YBCO over a finite range before being suppressed again at very small thicknesses.
method: The research employed Pulsed Laser Deposition (PLD) to fabricate $	ext{(Cu,C)-1234/YBCO}$ heterostructures and characterized them using four-probe electrical transport measurements as a function of film thickness.
model_or_system: The physical system is an epitaxial heterostructure composed of two cuprate superconductors: $	ext{YBCO}$ (bottom layer) and $	ext{(Cu,C)-1234}$ (top layer), grown on an LAO substrate. The study explores the superconducting coupling at this interface.
key_observables: Temperature-dependent resistance ($ho$-$T$ curves), superconducting transition temperature ($T_{c0}$), and normal state resistance as a function of film thickness.
important_parameters: Film thicknesses, particularly varying $	ext{(Cu,C)-1234}$ thickness from $188 	ext{ nm}$ down to $1.2 	ext{ nm}$.
main_assumptions: The observed recovery mechanism suggests that the robust superconducting state of YBCO helps reestablish long-range phase coherence in the ultrathin $	ext{(Cu,C)-1234}$ layer.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the growth process and test circuits; key results show how $T_{c0}$ drops with decreasing thickness for isolated films (SIT) but recovers when coupled to YBCO before dropping again at the thinnest limit.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure of fabrication ($	ext{PLD}$ growth), structural confirmation ($	ext{XRD}$, $	ext{STEM}/	ext{FFT}$), and systematic electrical characterization across varying thicknesses, comparing isolated film behavior to heterostructure performance.
why_interesting: This work provides experimental evidence on how interfacial coupling can stabilize superconductivity against intrinsic dimensional confinement effects in complex oxide systems, which is relevant for understanding quantum phase transitions in artificial superconducting junctions.
